summary_paragraph: A 78-year-old male with severe diastolic heart failure, severe aortic stenosis, atrial fibrillation, and recent MRSA pneumonia completed a course of vancomycin and presented for PICC line removal. He was found to be confused and fatigued, with lab results showing acute kidney injury, elevated BUN and creatinine, and worsening anemia. His symptoms were attributed to uremia from pre-renal azotemia due to aggressive diuresis. Diuretics were held for 36 hours, after which his kidney function improved, mental status returned to baseline, and anemia stabilized without intervention. He was discharged on adjusted medications, including reduced metoprolol and a modified torsemide regimen, with instructions to monitor weight and follow up with neurology for persistent myoclonic jerks.
